FJ1439.clinical: Weakness (foot drop) follows common fibular nerve injury; shin splints affect its attachment.

FJ1440.summary: The deepest muscle of the calf, its tendon passing behind the inner ankle.
FJ1440.function: Inverts and plantar flexes the foot and supports the medial arch.
FJ1440.clinical: Tendon failure leads to a progressive flat foot in adults.

FJ1461.summary: A thin muscle on the inside of the front of the rib cage.
FJ1461.function: Draws the costal cartilages down in expiration.

FJ1441.summary: The deep part of the quadriceps, lying on the front of the femur under rectus femoris.

FJ1442.summary: The largest part of the quadriceps, on the outer thigh.
FJ1442.clinical: Preferred site for intramuscular injections in infants.

FJ1443.summary: The part of the quadriceps on the inner thigh, bulging just above the knee.
FJ1443.function: Extends the knee and steadies the patella in its groove.
FJ1443.clinical: Wastes quickly after knee injury; strengthening it helps patellar tracking.

FJ2806.summary: The inner part of the thyroarytenoid lying beside the vocal ligament.
FJ2806.function: Fine-tunes the tension of the vocal fold.

FJ1549M.summary: Small muscles between the cervical transverse processes.

FJ1549.summary: Small muscles between the cervical transverse processes.

FJ1509M.summary: Four muscles between the metacarpals on the back of the hand.

FJ1509.summary: Four muscles between the metacarpals on the back of the hand.

FJ1552M.summary: Short paired muscles between the cervical spinous processes.
FJ1552M.function: Extend the neck and steady the vertebrae.

FJ1552.summary: Short paired muscles between the cervical spinous processes.
FJ1552.function: Extend the neck and steady the vertebrae.

FJ1550M.summary: Short muscles between the lumbar spinous processes.
FJ1550M.function: Extend and stabilise the lumbar spine.

FJ1550.summary: Short muscles between the lumbar spinous processes.
FJ1550.function: Extend and stabilise the lumbar spine.

FJ1462M.summary: Short muscles from the transverse processes to the rib below.

FJ1463M.summary: Longer muscles from the transverse processes skipping one rib.

FJ1510M.summary: Four slender muscles arising from the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.
FJ1510M.function: Flex the knuckles while extending the finger joints, the position for holding a pen.

FJ1510.summary: Four slender muscles arising from the tendons of flexor digitorum profundus.
FJ1510.function: Flex the knuckles while extending the finger joints, the position for holding a pen.

FJ1511M.summary: Three muscles between the metacarpals on the palm side.

FJ1511.summary: Three muscles between the metacarpals on the palm side.

FJ1553M.summary: Small muscles between the cervical transverse processes behind the spinal nerves.

FJ1553.summary: Small muscles between the cervical transverse processes behind the spinal nerves.

FJ1462.summary: Short muscles from the transverse processes to the rib below.

FJ1463.summary: Longer muscles from the transverse processes skipping one rib.

FJ1512M.summary: Short head of left biceps brachii is part of the biceps brachii. The two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm, from the scapula to the radius.
FJ1512M.function: Flexes the elbow and, most powerfully, supinates the forearm (turning the palm up).
FJ1512M.clinical: Rupture of the long head tendon produces a 'Popeye' bulge in the arm.

FJ1444M.summary: Short head of left biceps femoris is part of the biceps femoris. The lateral hamstring, with a long head from the ischium and a short head from the femur, inserting on the fibula.
FJ1444M.function: Flexes the knee and extends the hip; the main lateral rotator of the flexed knee.
FJ1444M.clinical: Hamstring tears are the commonest sprinting injury.

FJ1512.summary: Short head of right biceps brachii is part of the biceps brachii. The two-headed muscle on the front of the upper arm, from the scapula to the radius.
FJ1512.function: Flexes the elbow and, most powerfully, supinates the forearm (turning the palm up).
FJ1512.clinical: Rupture of the long head tendon produces a 'Popeye' bulge in the arm.

FJ1444.summary: Short head of right biceps femoris is part of the biceps femoris. The lateral hamstring, with a long head from the ischium and a short head from the femur, inserting on the fibula.
FJ1444.function: Flexes the knee and extends the hip; the main lateral rotator of the flexed knee.
FJ1444.clinical: Hamstring tears are the commonest sprinting injury.

FJ1513M.summary: Spinal part of left deltoid is part of the deltoid. The thick triangular muscle capping the shoulder, with clavicular, acromial and spinal parts.
FJ1513M.function: Its middle fibres abduct the arm; the front and back fibres flex and extend it.
FJ1513M.clinical: Common site for intramuscular injections; wasting follows axillary nerve injury.

FJ1513.summary: Spinal part of right deltoid is part of the deltoid. The thick triangular muscle capping the shoulder, with clavicular, acromial and spinal parts.
FJ1513.function: Its middle fibres abduct the arm; the front and back fibres flex and extend it.
FJ1513.clinical: Common site for intramuscular injections; wasting follows axillary nerve injury.

FJ1543M.summary: The medial column of the erector spinae, closest to the spinous processes.

FJ1543.summary: The medial column of the erector spinae, closest to the spinous processes.

FJ1464M.summary: Sternocostal part of left pectoralis major is part of the pectoralis major. The large fan-shaped muscle of the chest, with clavicular, sternocostal and abdominal parts.
FJ1464M.function: Adducts and medially rotates the arm and helps flex it; used in pushing and climbing.

FJ1464.summary: Sternocostal part of right pectoralis major is part of the pectoralis major. The large fan-shaped muscle of the chest, with clavicular, sternocostal and abdominal parts.
FJ1464.function: Adducts and medially rotates the arm and helps flex it; used in pushing and climbing.

FJ2783.summary: Straight part of left cricothyroid is part of the cricothyroid. A muscle on the outside of the larynx between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, the only laryngeal muscle supplied by the external laryngeal nerve.
FJ2783.function: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward to stretch the vocal ligaments and raise the pitch of the voice.

FJ2801.summary: Straight part of right cricothyroid is part of the cricothyroid. A muscle on the outside of the larynx between the cricoid and thyroid cartilages, the only laryngeal muscle supplied by the external laryngeal nerve.
FJ2801.function: Tilts the thyroid cartilage forward to stretch the vocal ligaments and raise the pitch of the voice.

FJ1514M.summary: Superficial head of left flexor pollicis brevis is part of the flexor pollicis brevis. A thenar muscle with a superficial and a deep head.
FJ1514M.function: Flexes the thumb at its base.

FJ1514.summary: Superficial head of right flexor pollicis brevis is part of the flexor pollicis brevis. A thenar muscle with a superficial and a deep head.
FJ1514.function: Flexes the thumb at its base.

FJ1600.summary: Superior oblique part of left longus colli is part of the longus colli. A deep muscle along the front of the cervical and upper thoracic vertebrae.
FJ1600.function: Flexes the neck and steadies the cervical spine.

FJ1465.summary: The thickened fascia on the inside of the pelvis from which the levator ani arises.

FJ1343.summary: Tendon of right levator palpebrae superioris is part of the levator palpebrae superioris. The muscle that raises the upper eyelid.
FJ1343.function: Opens the eye; its smooth-muscle part keeps the lid up in the alert state.
FJ1343.clinical: Weakness causes drooping of the eyelid (ptosis).

FJ1525M.summary: Deep rotator muscles of the thoracic spine, from transverse to spinous processes.
FJ1525M.function: Rotate and stabilise the vertebrae; rich in sensors that report spinal position.

FJ1525.summary: Deep rotator muscles of the thoracic spine, from transverse to spinous processes.
FJ1525.function: Rotate and stabilise the vertebrae; rich in sensors that report spinal position.

FJ2809.summary: An unpaired muscle joining the two arytenoid cartilages.
FJ2809.function: Closes the back of the glottis.

FJ1445M.summary: Transverse head of left adductor hallucis is part of the adductor hallucis. A muscle of the sole with an oblique and a transverse head inserting on the big toe.
FJ1445M.function: Adducts the big toe and supports the transverse arch.

FJ1515M.summary: Transverse head of left adductor pollicis is part of the adductor pollicis. A fan-shaped muscle in the web of the thumb with oblique and transverse heads.
FJ1515M.function: Adducts the thumb and gives the pinch its power.
FJ1515M.clinical: Weakness produces Froment's sign in ulnar nerve palsy.

FJ1445.summary: Transverse head of right adductor hallucis is part of the adductor hallucis. A muscle of the sole with an oblique and a transverse head inserting on the big toe.
FJ1445.function: Adducts the big toe and supports the transverse arch.

FJ1515.summary: Transverse head of right adductor pollicis is part of the adductor pollicis. A fan-shaped muscle in the web of the thumb with oblique and transverse heads.
FJ1515.function: Adducts the thumb and gives the pinch its power.
FJ1515.clinical: Weakness produces Froment's sign in ulnar nerve palsy.

FJ1554M.summary: Transverse part of left trapezius is part of the trapezius. The large kite-shaped muscle of the upper back and neck, with descending, transverse and ascending parts.
FJ1554M.function: Elevates, retracts and depresses the scapula and rotates it to raise the arm overhead.
FJ1554M.clinical: Its upper fibres carry much of the tension of neck and shoulder pain.

FJ1554.summary: Transverse part of right trapezius is part of the trapezius. The large kite-shaped muscle of the upper back and neck, with descending, transverse and ascending parts.
FJ1554.function: Elevates, retracts and depresses the scapula and rotates it to raise the arm overhead.
FJ1554.clinical: Its upper fibres carry much of the tension of neck and shoulder pain.

FJ1518M.summary: Ulnar head of left flexor carpi ulnaris is part of the flexor carpi ulnaris. The most medial forearm flexor, inserting on the pisiform.
FJ1518M.clinical: The ulnar nerve runs beneath it in the forearm.

FJ1516M.summary: Ulnar head of left pronator teres is part of the pronator teres. A muscle crossing the front of the forearm from the medial epicondyle and ulna to the radius.
FJ1516M.function: Pronates the forearm (turns the palm down) and helps flex the elbow.
FJ1516M.clinical: The median nerve passes between its two heads.

FJ1518.summary: Ulnar head of right flexor carpi ulnaris is part of the flexor carpi ulnaris. The most medial forearm flexor, inserting on the pisiform.
FJ1518.clinical: The ulnar nerve runs beneath it in the forearm.

FJ1516.summary: Ulnar head of right pronator teres is part of the pronator teres. A muscle crossing the front of the forearm from the medial epicondyle and ulna to the radius.
FJ1516.function: Pronates the forearm (turns the palm down) and helps flex the elbow.
FJ1516.clinical: The median nerve passes between its two heads.

FJ2762.summary: The small muscle inside the uvula.

FJ1601.summary: Vertical intermediate part of left longus colli is part of the longus colli. A deep muscle along the front of the cervical and upper thoracic vertebrae.
FJ1601.function: Flexes the neck and steadies the cervical spine.

FJ2420.summary: The larger of the two leaflets of the mitral valve between the left atrium and ventricle.
FJ2420.function: Swings shut during ventricular contraction to stop blood flowing back into the atrium.

FJ2421.summary: The largest leaflet of the tricuspid valve between the right atrium and ventricle.

FJ2419.summary: The largest papillary muscle of the right ventricle.
FJ2419.function: Its chordae tendineae stop the tricuspid leaflets flipping back into the atrium.

FJ2418.summary: A head of the anterolateral papillary muscle of the left ventricle.

FJ2425.summary: The chamber receiving oxygenated blood from the pulmonary veins.

FJ2422.summary: The chamber of the left ventricle, which pumps blood into the aorta.
FJ2422.clinical: Its ejection fraction is the standard measure of heart function.

FJ2424.summary: The chamber receiving deoxygenated blood from the body.

FJ2423.summary: The chamber of the right ventricle, which pumps blood into the pulmonary trunk.

FJ2429.summary: One of the two large papillary muscles of the left ventricle anchoring the mitral valve.
FJ2429.clinical: Rupture after a heart attack causes sudden severe mitral regurgitation.

FJ2417.summary: One of the three half-moon cusps of the pulmonary valve at the outlet of the right ventricle.
FJ2417.function: Prevents blood returning from the pulmonary trunk during diastole.

FJ2427.summary: One of the three cusps of the pulmonary valve.

FJ2432.summary: The smaller, crescent-shaped leaflet of the mitral valve.
FJ2432.function: Meets the anterior leaflet to seal the valve.

FJ2433.summary: One of the three leaflets of the tricuspid valve.

FJ2430.summary: A papillary muscle on the floor of the right ventricle anchoring the tricuspid valve.

FJ2434.summary: One of the three half-moon cusps of the pulmonary valve at the outlet of the right ventricle.
FJ2434.function: Prevents blood returning from the pulmonary trunk during diastole.

FJ2436.summary: The leaflet of the tricuspid valve attached to the interventricular septum.

FJ2437.summary: A small papillary muscle arising from the septum of the right ventricle.

FJ2438.summary: The thin muscular wall of the left atrium, which receives oxygenated blood from the four pulmonary veins.
FJ2438.function: Contracts to top up the left ventricle just before it pumps.
FJ2438.clinical: Atrial fibrillation can let clots form here, a major cause of stroke.

FJ2439.summary: The wall of the right atrium, which receives venous blood from the venae cavae and coronary sinus.
FJ2439.function: Houses the sinoatrial node, the heart's natural pacemaker.

FJ2428.summary: The thick muscular walls of the two ventricles and the septum between them; the left wall is about three times thicker than the right.
FJ2428.function: Contract to pump blood to the lungs (right) and the body (left).
FJ2428.clinical: Heart attacks damage this muscle; the left ventricle thickens in high blood pressure.

FJ1932.summary: The aorta from the diaphragm to its division into the common iliac arteries at L4.
FJ1932.function: Supplies the abdominal organs, kidneys and the lower limbs.
FJ1932.clinical: Abdominal aortic aneurysms are screened for in older men.

FJ3009.summary: Accessory subsuperior branch of right posterior basal segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ2211.summary: Acromial branch of left thoraco-acromial artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2211.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2263.summary: Acromial branch of right thoraco-acromial artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2263.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2982.summary: Anterior branch of lateral segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ2975.summary: Anterior branch of right anterior segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ2978.summary: Anterior part of right apical segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ1661M.summary: Anterior temporal branch of left lateral occipital artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1661M.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1661.summary: Anterior temporal branch of right lateral occipital artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1661.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1662M.summary: Anterolateral central branch of left middle cerebral artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1662M.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1662.summary: Anterolateral central branch of right middle cerebral artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1662.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2967.summary: Apical part of right apical segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ2968.summary: Apical part of right posterior segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ3411.summary: The curved part of the aorta arching over the heart and left main bronchus.
FJ3411.function: Gives rise to the brachiocephalic trunk, left common carotid and left subclavian arteries.
FJ3411.clinical: Contains baroreceptors that sense blood pressure.

FJ3413.summary: The first 5 cm of the aorta, rising from the left ventricle behind the pulmonary trunk.
FJ3413.function: Gives off the two coronary arteries just above the aortic valve.
FJ3413.clinical: Aortic dissection most often begins here.

FJ3414.summary: Ascending branch of inferior branch of ileocolic artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ3414.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ3399.summary: Ascending branch of left colic artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ3399.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ3002.summary: Basal branch of right anterior basal segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ1672.summary: The single artery formed by the two vertebral arteries on the front of the pons.
FJ1672.function: Supplies the brainstem, cerebellum and occipital lobes.

FJ3417.summary: The first branch of the aortic arch, dividing into the right common carotid and right subclavian arteries.

FJ1673M.summary: Branch of left middle cerebral artery to left angular gyrus: a fold of the cerebral cortex bounded by sulci, part of the surface of the cerebral hemisphere.
FJ1673M.function: Cortical grey matter processing sensation, movement, language or memory depending on its location.

FJ1673.summary: Branch of right middle cerebral artery to right angular gyrus: a fold of the cerebral cortex bounded by sulci, part of the surface of the cerebral hemisphere.
FJ1673.function: Cortical grey matter processing sensation, movement, language or memory depending on its location.

FJ3077.summary: Caudate lobe branch of left hepatic artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ3077.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1916.summary: Caudate lobe branch of right hepatic artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1916.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ3421.summary: The first major branch of the abdominal aorta, dividing into the left gastric, splenic and common hepatic arteries.
FJ3421.function: Supplies the stomach, liver, spleen, pancreas and duodenum.

FJ2649.summary: The branch of the left coronary curving round the left side of the heart.
FJ2649.function: Supplies the lateral and back wall of the left ventricle.

FJ3078.summary: A branch of the coeliac trunk supplying the liver, gallbladder, stomach and duodenum.

FJ2643.summary: Conus branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2643.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2230.summary: Deltoid branch of left thoraco-acromial artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2230.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2282.summary: Deltoid branch of right thoraco-acromial artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2282.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ3427.summary: The aorta beyond the arch, descending through the chest and abdomen to its division at L4.
FJ3427.function: Supplies the chest wall, abdominal organs and lower limbs through its branches.

FJ3428.summary: Descending branch of left colic artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ3428.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2063.summary: Descending branch of left lateral circumflex femoral artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2063.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2057.summary: Descending branch of right lateral circumflex femoral artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2057.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1931.summary: The descending aorta as it runs down the chest beside the vertebral column.
FJ1931.function: Supplies the chest wall, oesophagus and bronchi through its branches.

FJ2633.summary: Diagonal branch of anterior descending branch of left coronary artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2633.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2231.summary: Dorsal carpal branch of left radial artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2231.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2283.summary: Dorsal carpal branch of right radial artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2283.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2072.summary: Dorsal digital artery of foot: one of the small vessels running along the digits.
FJ2072.function: Supplies the skin and tissues of the fingers or toes.

FJ2671.summary: First anterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2671.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2714.summary: First posterior ventricular branch of right coronary artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2714.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2632.summary: First right anterior branch of anterior interventricular branch of left coronary artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2632.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2735.summary: First septal branch of right posterior interventricular artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2735.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ3081.summary: The artery entering the liver alongside the portal vein and bile duct.
FJ3081.function: Provides about a quarter of the liver's blood supply, rich in oxygen.

FJ1679M.summary: Hypothalamic branch of left posterior communicating artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1679M.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1679.summary: Hypothalamic branch of right posterior communicating artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ1679.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2034.summary: Ileal branch of inferior branch of ileocolic artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2034.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2987.summary: Inferior branch of medial segmental artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ2896.summary: Inferior lingular artery: a branch serving one segment of the lung.

FJ3442.summary: The artery supplying the descending and sigmoid colon and the rectum.

FJ2049.summary: Inferior segmental branch of left renal artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2049.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ2043.summary: Inferior segmental branch of right renal artery: a branch of its parent vessel.
FJ2043.function: Distributes blood to the tissues along its course.

FJ1816.function: Passes sound signals to the auditory cortex.

FJ1788.summary: The middle gyrus of the lateral frontal lobe.
FJ1788.function: Working memory, attention and eye movement control (frontal eye field).

FJ1790.summary: The middle gyrus of the lateral temporal lobe.
FJ1790.function: Contributes to word meaning, face recognition and visual motion perception.

FJ1361.summary: A branch of the ophthalmic nerve crossing the orbit to the nose.
FJ1361.function: Sensation from the eyeball, the nasal cavity and the skin of the nose.

FJ1792.summary: The lobe at the back of the brain.
FJ1792.function: The visual cortex: interprets everything the eyes see.
FJ1792.clinical: Damage causes loss of the opposite visual field.

FJ1363.summary: The first division of the trigeminal nerve, entering the orbit.
FJ1363.function: Carries sensation from the eye, forehead, upper eyelid and nose.
FJ1363.clinical: Shingles in this nerve can involve the eye.

FJ1364.summary: The second cranial nerve, carrying about a million fibres from the retina to the optic chiasm.
FJ1364.function: Transmits vision from the eye to the brain.
FJ1364.clinical: Optic neuritis, often the first sign of multiple sclerosis, and glaucoma damage its fibres.

FJ1820.summary: The visual pathway from the chiasm to the lateral geniculate body.
FJ1820.function: Carries the opposite visual field to the thalamus.

FJ1786.summary: The gyrus on the medial temporal lobe surrounding the hippocampus.
FJ1786.function: Memory encoding and the recognition of scenes.

FJ1798.summary: The gyrus behind the central sulcus: the primary somatosensory cortex.
FJ1798.function: Receives touch, pressure, pain and position sense from the opposite side of the body.

FJ1366.summary: A small branch of the nasociliary nerve to the ethmoidal and sphenoidal sinuses.

FJ1801.summary: The gyrus in front of the central sulcus: the primary motor cortex.
FJ1801.function: Sends the commands for voluntary movement of the opposite side of the body, mapped as the motor homunculus.
FJ1801.clinical: Damage causes weakness (upper motor neuron signs) on the opposite side.

FJ1823.summary: The outer part of the lentiform nucleus of the basal ganglia.
FJ1823.function: Regulates movement together with the caudate nucleus.
FJ1823.clinical: A common site of hypertensive brain haemorrhage.

FJ1824.summary: A fibre bundle running along the top of the thalamus to the habenula.

FJ1826.summary: The upper of the two bumps on the back of the midbrain.
FJ1826.function: Directs the eyes and head toward visual stimuli.

FJ1834.summary: The uppermost of the three frontal gyri.
FJ1834.function: Involved in planning, self-awareness and the supplementary motor area.

FJ1836.summary: The upper part of the parietal lobe behind the postcentral gyrus.
FJ1836.function: Spatial awareness and guiding movements with the eyes and hands.

FJ1376.summary: A branch of the frontal nerve leaving the orbit through the supraorbital notch.
FJ1376.function: Sensation from the forehead and front of the scalp.

FJ1842.summary: A gyrus of the inferior parietal lobule curling over the end of the lateral fissure.
FJ1842.function: Language, touch perception and body awareness.

FJ1377.summary: A branch of the frontal nerve passing above the trochlea.
FJ1377.function: Sensation from the middle of the forehead and upper eyelid.

FJ1827.summary: A pair of egg-shaped masses of grey matter deep in the brain on either side of the third ventricle.
FJ1827.function: The gateway to the cortex: almost every sensory pathway is relayed here, and it regulates consciousness and attention.
FJ1827.clinical: Thalamic stroke can produce loss of sensation or chronic pain on the opposite side.

FJ1381.summary: The fourth cranial nerve, the thinnest and the only one emerging from the back of the brainstem.
FJ1381.function: Supplies the superior oblique muscle of the eye.
FJ1381.clinical: Palsy causes vertical double vision, worst when looking down stairs.

FJ1832.summary: The septal region at the front of the brain below the corpus callosum.
FJ1832.function: Part of the reward and emotion circuits of the limbic system.

FJ1319.summary: Small nerves from the ciliary ganglion to the eyeball.
FJ1319.function: Carry parasympathetic fibres that constrict the pupil and focus the lens.

FJ1825.summary: A slender fibre bundle from the amygdala following the curve of the caudate nucleus.
FJ1825.function: Carries output from the amygdala to the hypothalamus.

FJ1321.summary: The upper division of the third cranial nerve.
FJ1321.function: Supplies the superior rectus and the levator of the upper eyelid.

FJ1372.summary: The upper division of the third cranial nerve.
FJ1372.function: Supplies the superior rectus and the levator of the upper eyelid.

FJ1843.summary: The tent-shaped fold of dura mater separating the cerebellum from the occipital lobes.
FJ1843.clinical: A swelling brain can herniate through its opening, compressing the brainstem.

FJ1730.summary: The narrow midline cavity between the two thalami.
FJ1730.function: Passes cerebrospinal fluid from the lateral ventricles to the aqueduct.

FJ1780.summary: The grey hump of the hypothalamus from which the pituitary stalk arises.
FJ1780.function: Releases the hormones that control the anterior pituitary.

FJ1758.summary: The mass of myelinated fibres beneath the cortex.
FJ1758.function: Connects cortical areas with each other and with the rest of the nervous system.
FJ1758.clinical: Multiple sclerosis attacks white matter myelin.

FJ1806.summary: The mass of myelinated fibres beneath the cortex.
FJ1806.function: Connects cortical areas with each other and with the rest of the nervous system.
FJ1806.clinical: Multiple sclerosis attacks white matter myelin.

FJ1282.summary: The fluid-filled space between the cornea and the iris.
FJ1282.function: Filled with aqueous humour that nourishes the cornea and lens.
FJ1282.clinical: Blocked drainage of aqueous humour raises pressure in glaucoma.

FJ1332.summary: The fluid-filled space between the cornea and the iris.
FJ1332.function: Filled with aqueous humour that nourishes the cornea and lens.
FJ1332.clinical: Blocked drainage of aqueous humour raises pressure in glaucoma.

FJ2811.summary: The auricle (pinna): the visible ear of skin-covered elastic cartilage.
FJ2811.function: Collects sound and funnels it into the ear canal; its shape helps locate sounds.

FJ1285.summary: The vascular layer between the sclera and retina.
FJ1285.function: Nourishes the outer retina and absorbs stray light with its pigment.

FJ1289.summary: The transparent dome at the front of the eye.
FJ1289.function: Provides about two thirds of the eye's focusing power; it has no blood vessels and is densely supplied with pain fibres.
FJ1289.clinical: Scratches heal quickly but ulcers can scar; laser surgery reshapes it to correct vision.

FJ1287.summary: The folded front part of the ciliary body behind the iris.
FJ1287.function: Produces aqueous humour and suspends the lens.

FJ1297.summary: The coloured ring of muscle in front of the lens.
FJ1297.function: Adjusts the pupil to control how much light enters the eye.

FJ1298.summary: A tiny channel draining tears from the eyelid margin to the lacrimal sac.

FJ1299.summary: The almond-shaped gland in the upper outer corner of the orbit.
FJ1299.function: Produces tears that wash and protect the eye.

FJ1301.summary: The pool of tears in the inner corner of the eye.

FJ1309.summary: The upper dilated part of the tear drainage duct in the inner orbit.
FJ1309.clinical: Infection (dacryocystitis) causes a painful swelling beside the nose.

FJ1305.summary: The transparent, elastic disc behind the iris.
FJ1305.function: Changes shape to focus on near or distant objects.
FJ1305.clinical: Clouding of the lens (cataract) is the commonest cause of treatable blindness.

FJ1302.summary: The duct carrying tears from the lacrimal sac into the nose.
FJ1302.clinical: Blockage causes a constantly watering eye.

FJ1317.summary: The tough white outer coat of the eyeball.
FJ1317.function: Protects the eye, keeps its shape and anchors the extraocular muscles.

FJ1331.summary: The clear jelly filling the back of the eyeball.
FJ1331.function: Keeps the eyeball inflated and holds the retina in place.
FJ1331.clinical: Its shrinking with age causes floaters and can tear the retina.

FJ1316.summary: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye.
FJ1316.function: Rods and cones convert light into nerve signals sent along the optic nerve.
FJ1316.clinical: Retinal detachment, diabetic retinopathy and macular degeneration.

FJ1367.summary: The light-sensitive layer lining the back of the eye.
FJ1367.function: Rods and cones convert light into nerve signals sent along the optic nerve.
FJ1367.clinical: Retinal detachment, diabetic retinopathy and macular degeneration.

FJ2440.function: Supports the larynx and the arytenoid cartilages that move the vocal folds.
FJ2440.clinical: Pressure on the cricoid can compress the oesophagus during emergency intubation.

FJ2770.summary: A leaf-shaped flap of elastic cartilage behind the tongue.
FJ2770.function: Folds down over the larynx during swallowing to keep food out of the airway.
FJ2770.clinical: Acute epiglottitis can obstruct the airway.

FJ2771.summary: An elastic band from the hyoid bone to the epiglottis.

FJ2449.summary: Lateral segmental bronchial tree: the airway branch serving one bronchopulmonary segment, a self-contained wedge of lung with its own artery.
FJ2449.function: Conducts air to the alveoli of its segment; surgeons can remove a single segment along this boundary.

FJ2535.summary: Left anterior basal segmental bronchial tree: the airway branch serving one bronchopulmonary segment, a self-contained wedge of lung with its own artery.

FJ2775.summary: A pyramid-shaped cartilage on top of the cricoid.

FJ2776.summary: A small nodule of cartilage on the apex of each arytenoid.

FJ2786.function: Suspends the larynx from the hyoid; the internal laryngeal nerve pierces it.

FJ2787.summary: The elastic core of the vocal fold, from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid.
FJ2787.function: Vibrates in the airstream to produce the voice.

FJ2451.summary: Medial segmental bronchial tree: the airway branch serving one bronchopulmonary segment, a self-contained wedge of lung with its own artery.
FJ2451.function: Conducts air to the alveoli of its segment; surgeons can remove a single segment along this boundary.

FJ2789.summary: The midline part of the cricothyroid membrane.
FJ2789.clinical: The site for emergency cricothyroidotomy when the airway is blocked above.

FJ2452.summary: Right anterior basal segmental bronchial tree: the airway branch serving one bronchopulmonary segment, a self-contained wedge of lung with its own artery.
FJ2452.function: Conducts air to the alveoli of its segment; surgeons can remove a single segment along this boundary.

FJ2454.function: Conducts air to the alveoli of its segment; surgeons can remove a single segment along this boundary.

FJ2539.function: Conducts air to the right lung.
FJ2539.clinical: Inhaled objects usually lodge in the right main bronchus because of its straighter course.

FJ2554.summary: A U-shaped cartilage surrounding the nostril and forming the nasal tip.

FJ2459.function: Conducts air to the alveoli of its segment; surgeons can remove a single segment along this boundary.

FJ2804.summary: A sheet of fibrous tissue joining the thyroid cartilage to the hyoid bone.
FJ2804.function: Suspends the larynx from the hyoid; the internal laryngeal nerve pierces it.

FJ2805.summary: The elastic core of the vocal fold, from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid.
FJ2805.function: Vibrates in the airstream to produce the voice.

FJ2557.summary: The cartilage of the nasal septum in front of the vomer and ethmoid.
FJ2557.function: Divides the nostrils and supports the nose.
FJ2557.clinical: Deviation causes blockage; septoplasty straightens it.

FJ2807.summary: A ligament fixing the stalk of the epiglottis to the thyroid cartilage.

FJ2808.summary: The largest laryngeal cartilage, whose front angle forms the Adam's apple.
FJ2808.function: Shields the larynx and anchors the vocal ligaments.

FJ2541.summary: The windpipe: a tube about 11 cm long, held open by C-shaped cartilage rings, from the larynx to the bronchi.
FJ2541.function: Conducts air to and from the lungs while its lining traps and sweeps out dust.
FJ2541.clinical: A tracheostomy opens the trachea below the larynx to secure the airway.

FJ2565.summary: A blind-ended worm-like tube hanging from the caecum.
FJ2565.function: Contains lymphoid tissue; its role in digestion is negligible.
FJ2565.clinical: Appendicitis is the commonest cause of emergency abdominal surgery.

FJ2566.summary: The part of the large intestine rising up the right side of the abdomen from the caecum.
FJ2566.function: Absorbs water and salts from the intestinal contents.

FJ2816.summary: A small lobe on the back of the liver between the vena cava and the ligamentum venosum (segment I).
FJ2816.function: Drains directly into the inferior vena cava, so it is spared in some liver diseases.

FJ3079.summary: The duct formed by the union of the right and left hepatic ducts, carrying bile out of the liver.

FJ3080.summary: The short duct joining the gallbladder to the common bile duct.

FJ2567.summary: The part of the colon running down the left side of the abdomen.
FJ2567.function: Stores faeces before they pass into the sigmoid colon.
FJ2567.clinical: Diverticular disease and cancer are commoner on the left side of the colon.

FJ2587.summary: Distal part of ileum: a length of the ileum, the last part of the small intestine, modelled as several coils.
FJ2587.function: Absorbs nutrients across a vast folded surface; the ileum also absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.

FJ2611.summary: Distal part of jejunum: a length of the jejunum, the second part of the small intestine, modelled as several coils.
FJ2611.function: Absorbs nutrients across a vast folded surface; the ileum also absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.

FJ2573.summary: The first, C-shaped part of the small intestine, curving around the head of the pancreas.
FJ2573.function: Receives chyme, bile and pancreatic juice and neutralises stomach acid.
FJ2573.clinical: The commonest site of peptic ulcers.

FJ2563.summary: The oesophagus: a 25 cm muscular tube carrying food from the pharynx through the chest to the stomach.
FJ2563.function: Peristaltic waves push swallowed food downward; the lower sphincter stops stomach acid returning.
FJ2563.clinical: Reflux, Barrett's oesophagus and oesophageal cancer; swallowing difficulty (dysphagia) needs investigation.

FJ2817.summary: A pear-shaped sac beneath the liver storing about 50 ml of bile.
FJ2817.function: Concentrates bile and squirts it into the duodenum when fatty food arrives.
FJ2817.clinical: Gallstones can cause colic, cholecystitis and jaundice; removal (cholecystectomy) is one of the commonest operations.

FJ1253.summary: The gums surrounding the lower teeth.
FJ1253.function: Seal the teeth against the jaw and resist chewing forces.

FJ1252.summary: The gums surrounding the upper teeth.
FJ1252.function: Seal the teeth against the jaw and resist chewing forces.
FJ1252.clinical: Gingivitis and periodontitis are among the commonest diseases worldwide.

FJ2599.summary: Where the ileum enters the caecum, guarded by the ileocaecal valve.
FJ2599.function: Regulates flow into the large intestine and prevents backflow.

FJ3094.summary: A bile duct draining the caudate lobe.

FJ3096.summary: The duct draining bile from the left half of the liver.

FJ2765.summary: The smallest of the major salivary glands, under the tongue.
FJ2765.function: Secretes thick, mucous saliva through many small ducts.

FJ2766.summary: A walnut-sized salivary gland beneath the jaw.
FJ2766.function: Produces most of the saliva at rest, opening beneath the tongue.
FJ2766.clinical: The commonest site of salivary stones.

FJ2814.summary: The fleshy folds surrounding the mouth.
FJ2814.function: Seal the mouth, hold food and shape speech and expression.

FJ3396.summary: The fan-shaped fold of peritoneum that suspends the jejunum and ileum from the back wall of the abdomen.
FJ3396.function: Carries the vessels, nerves and lymphatics of the small intestine.
FJ3396.clinical: Twisting of the mesentery (volvulus) cuts off the blood supply to the bowel.

FJ3397.summary: The small fold of peritoneum carrying the appendicular artery to the appendix.

FJ2576.summary: Middle part of ileum: a length of the ileum, the last part of the small intestine, modelled as several coils.
FJ2576.function: Absorbs nutrients across a vast folded surface; the ileum also absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.

FJ2607.summary: Middle part of jejunum: a length of the jejunum, the second part of the small intestine, modelled as several coils.
FJ2607.function: Absorbs nutrients across a vast folded surface; the ileum also absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.

FJ1895.summary: A soft, elongated gland lying across the back of the abdomen behind the stomach.
FJ1895.function: Its exocrine tissue makes enzymes for digesting fat, protein and starch; its islets secrete insulin and glucagon.
FJ1895.clinical: Pancreatitis, pancreatic cancer and type 1 diabetes.

FJ1896.summary: The main duct running the length of the pancreas to the duodenum.
FJ1896.function: Carries pancreatic juice to the duodenum, usually joining the bile duct at the ampulla.
FJ1896.clinical: Blockage by a stone or tumour causes pancreatitis or jaundice.

FJ2630.summary: The branching system of ducts collecting enzyme-rich juice from the pancreatic lobules.

FJ2629.summary: The glandular tissue of the pancreas.
FJ2629.function: Produces digestive enzymes and the hormones of the islets.

FJ2574.summary: Proximal part of ileum: a length of the ileum, the last part of the small intestine, modelled as several coils.
FJ2574.function: Absorbs nutrients across a vast folded surface; the ileum also absorbs vitamin B12 and bile salts.

FJ2606.summary: Proximal part of jejunum: a length of the jejunum, the second part of the small intestine, modelled as several coils.

FJ2571.summary: The final 12 cm of the large intestine, in the pelvis in front of the sacrum.
FJ2571.function: Stores faeces and signals the need to defecate.
FJ2571.clinical: Rectal bleeding and change of bowel habit are warning signs of colorectal cancer.

FJ3123.summary: The duct draining bile from the right half of the liver.

FJ2767.summary: The smallest of the major salivary glands, under the tongue.

FJ2768.clinical: The commonest site of salivary stones.

FJ2564.function: Begins protein digestion, kills microbes with acid and releases chyme into the duodenum in measured amounts.
FJ2564.clinical: Peptic ulcers (often from Helicobacter pylori), gastritis and gastric cancer.

FJ2568.summary: One of the three longitudinal bands of muscle on the colon, the free band not attached to mesentery.
FJ2568.function: Shortens the colon into its pouches (haustra).

FJ2569.summary: The longitudinal muscle band of the colon along the attachment of the mesocolon.

FJ2570.summary: The longitudinal muscle band of the colon along the attachment of the greater omentum.

FJ2761.summary: A muscular organ in the floor of the mouth covered with taste buds.
FJ2761.function: Moves food, shapes speech and senses taste; the genioglossus keeps it from falling back in sleep.
FJ2761.clinical: Oral cancers commonly arise on the side of the tongue.

FJ2572.summary: The longest, most mobile part of the colon, hanging across the abdomen below the stomach.
FJ2572.function: Continues water absorption and moves stool toward the descending colon.

FJ3398.summary: The fold of peritoneum suspending the transverse colon from the back wall of the abdomen.

FJ3145.summary: A bean-shaped organ on the back wall of the abdomen; the left lies slightly higher than the right.
FJ3145.function: Filters the blood to form urine, balances water and salts, regulates blood pressure and makes erythropoietin.
FJ3145.clinical: Kidney stones, infections and chronic kidney disease; a single healthy kidney is enough for normal life.

FJ3144.summary: A 25 cm muscular tube from the renal pelvis to the bladder.
FJ3144.function: Peristalsis carries urine to the bladder; the ureter tunnels obliquely into the bladder wall to prevent backflow.
FJ3144.clinical: Stones lodging in the ureter cause severe colicky pain.

FJ3148.summary: The tube carrying urine from the bladder out of the body; in the male it also carries semen and runs about 20 cm through the prostate and penis.
FJ3148.clinical: Urethral strictures and injuries; the prostatic part is compressed in prostatic enlargement.

FJ3149.summary: A hollow muscular organ in the pelvis that stores urine.
FJ3149.function: Expands to hold about 400 to 600 ml, then contracts (the detrusor) to empty through the urethra.
FJ3149.clinical: Urinary tract infections, overactive bladder and bladder cancer.

FJ3132.summary: One of the two erectile cylinders along the top of the penis.
FJ3132.function: Fills with blood to produce an erection.

FJ3133.summary: The erectile body surrounding the urethra, ending in the glans.
FJ3133.function: Keeps the urethra open during erection.

FJ3134.summary: The expanded sensitive tip of the penis, formed by the corpus spongiosum.

FJ3135.summary: The vas deferens: a thick-walled tube carrying sperm from the epididymis through the inguinal canal to the ejaculatory duct.

FJ3136.summary: A tightly coiled tube on the back of the testis.
FJ3136.function: Stores sperm while they mature and gain the ability to swim.

FJ3137.summary: A coiled gland behind the bladder.
FJ3137.function: Produces most of the volume of semen, rich in fructose.

FJ3138.summary: The male gonad, suspended in the scrotum where it is cooler than the body core.
FJ3138.clinical: Testicular torsion is an emergency; testicular cancer mostly affects young men.

FJ3139.summary: A walnut-sized gland surrounding the first part of the urethra below the bladder.
FJ3139.function: Secretes fluid that makes up about a third of semen.
FJ3139.clinical: Benign enlargement slows the urinary stream in older men; prostate cancer is among the commonest male cancers.

FJ3140.summary: The vas deferens: a thick-walled tube carrying sperm from the epididymis through the inguinal canal to the ejaculatory duct.

FJ3141.function: Stores sperm while they mature and gain the ability to swim.

FJ3143.function: Produces most of the volume of semen, rich in fructose.

FJ3142.summary: The male gonad, suspended in the scrotum where it is cooler than the body core.
FJ3142.clinical: Testicular torsion is an emergency; testicular cancer mostly affects young men.

FJ3129.summary: A small triangular gland sitting on top of the kidney.
FJ3129.function: The cortex makes cortisol, aldosterone and androgens; the medulla releases adrenaline in stress.
FJ3129.clinical: Addison's disease (failure) and Cushing's syndrome (excess cortisol).

FJ1796.summary: A pea-sized gland hanging from the hypothalamus in a bony hollow of the sphenoid.
FJ1796.function: The 'master gland': controls growth, thyroid, adrenal and reproductive function and water balance.
FJ1796.clinical: Pituitary tumours can press on the optic chiasm, narrowing the visual fields.

FJ3130.summary: A small triangular gland sitting on top of the kidney.
FJ3130.function: The cortex makes cortisol, aldosterone and androgens; the medulla releases adrenaline in stress.
FJ3130.clinical: Addison's disease (failure) and Cushing's syndrome (excess cortisol).

FJ3150.summary: One of the two lobes of the thymus behind the sternum.
FJ3150.function: Trains T lymphocytes in childhood; the gland shrinks after puberty.

FJ3151.summary: One of the two lobes of the thymus behind the sternum.
FJ3151.function: Trains T lymphocytes in childhood; the gland shrinks after puberty.

FJ2561.summary: A soft, fist-sized organ in the upper left abdomen under the ribs.
FJ2561.function: Filters the blood, removes worn-out red cells and mounts immune responses to blood-borne infection.
FJ2561.clinical: Ruptures in abdominal trauma; people without a spleen need vaccination against encapsulated bacteria.

FJ2812.summary: The arch of hair above each eye.
FJ2812.function: Diverts sweat and rain away from the eye and plays a large role in facial expression.

FJ2813.summary: The scalp hair, modelled as a single surface.
FJ2813.function: Insulates the scalp and protects it from sunlight.

FJ2815.summary: Hair of the pubic region, a secondary sexual characteristic that appears at puberty.

FJ2810.summary: The outer covering of the body and its largest organ, shown here as a translucent shell.
FJ2810.function: Barrier against infection and water loss, the organ of touch and temperature sensation, and a regulator of body heat.
FJ2810.clinical: Wounds, burns, infections and skin cancers all begin at this surface.
